thread:
Jia Chen: Heads-up — I brought up hera-embed-2 (3B) on the dev eval cluster and ran the standard holdout + recall suite. Did PTQ int8 per-channel with the calibration set from our news_pair_holdout.
Samir Patel: Nice. Any large regressions vs the fp16 baseline? :eyes:
Jia Chen: FP16 baseline recall@1=0.78, recall@5=0.91 on news_pair_holdout. After PTQ int8 per-channel: recall@1=0.67, recall@5=0.86. silhouette dropped from 0.42 -> 0.29. Also cosine drift seen on short queries.
Ava Morales: Oof. Is that consistent across datasets or specific to news? How about multilingual analogs?
Jia Chen: Quick sweep: wiki_holdout recall@1 0.74 -> 0.73 (small), faq_holdout 0.81 -> 0.76 (moderate), news was worst. Seems sensitive to short-text length distribution and high-IDF tokens.
Ravi Kapoor: Did you use per-channel minmax or symmetric quant? Any calibrator details?
Jia Chen: Used PTQ per-channel symmetric with 2048 calibration samples, clip at 99.9th percentile. Command:
```
run_eval --model hera-embed-2 --quant int8_perchannel --calib_samples 2048 --calib_clip 0.999 --datasets news_pair_holdout,wiki_holdout,faq_holdout --metrics recall@1,recall@5,silhouette
```
ml-eval-bot: Eval job 2026-02-18-0023 completed: 3 datasets, 2048 calib. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/hera-embed-2/1758004321/
Samir Patel: Can you dump some nearest-neighbor examples where it fails? Maybe KV-cache or tokenization mismatch? Also include raw L2/cosine distributions.
Jia Chen: Attached quick example top1 mismatch (news):
- Query: "election turnout declines"
- FP16 top1: doc_342 (related: turnout analysis)
- PTQ top1: doc_819 (unrelated: polling station logistics)
Cosine scores: fp16 0.84 vs int8 0.72. Distances shift non-uniformly.
Ava Morales: Try two quick experiments: 1) per-tensor symmetric PTQ, 2) use 4096 calibration samples with per-channel. For (2) maybe clip at 0.9995. Also attempt JS divergence on token distributions between calib and holdout.
Jia Chen: Will run both. Also plan to try 8-bit LLM-adaptive quant (QLoRA-style) vs PTQ to compare.
Ravi Kapoor: If per-tensor reduces variance but hurts overall, we can consider mixing: per-channel for shortlist layers, per-tensor for output proj. Any perf impact estimates?
Jia Chen: int8 per-channel gives ~2.9x throughput vs fp16 on A100. Adding mixed scheme probably still >2.5x. I'll log throughput numbers.
ml-eval-bot: New eval queued: 1758005120 (per-tensor) and 1758005205 (per-channel 4096calib). ETA ~15m.
Samir Patel: Also add clustering stability check: run UMAP + DBSCAN and compare cluster purity on labeled subset. If clusters scramble, that's a red flag.
Jia Chen: Yep adding that. Will post results in this thread when jobs finish. Thanks :thumbsup:
